description: Earth reference windows from ETOPO 2022 (60 and 15 arc-seconds) shown beside regional maps at the same metres per pixel. Comparison inputs only, never forcing. box is [west, south, east, north] in degrees (west > east crosses the date line), centre is [lon, lat], metres_per_pixel is [min, max] where the features show. There is no water mask: the largest lakes carry their bed (Lake Superior to -180 m, the Caspian), most others a flat surface (checked on the 15 arc-second tiles: Geneva, Garda, Como, Constance, General Carrera, Lake of the Woods, Nipigon); ground below 0 m connected to the window's edge is drawn as sea, enclosed basins below 0 m as land; no rivers or ice are marked.

windows.name: zagros
windows.title: Zagros simply folded belt, Iran
features: whaleback (periclinal) anticlines 10-20 km apart and 50-150 km long, en echelon, parallel to the belt's NW-SE trend
eroded anticline cores: breached crests with inward-facing flatirons and inverted relief
salt plugs (Hormuz salt diapirs) as round domes a few km across in the Fars arc and on the Gulf coast
the High Zagros and the Main Zagros Reverse Fault as the belt's highest, northeastern edge above 3 km
the Dezful embayment and the Mesopotamian foreland as flat lowland to the southwest
the Kazerun fault's north-south offset of the fold trains near 51.5 E
the Persian Gulf as a shallow (under 100 m) foreland sea

windows.name: eastern_tibet_three_rivers
windows.title: Eastern Tibet and the Three Parallel Rivers
features: the Salween, Mekong and Yangtze (Jinsha) gorges running north-south within about 70 km of each other, 2-3 km deep
the low-relief plateau surface at 4-5 km between and north of the gorges
the Longmen Shan front rising about 4 km over 50 km above the flat Sichuan Basin near 31 N, 103-104 E
Gongga Shan (7.5 km) on the plateau's eastern margin near 29.6 N, 101.9 E
the Red River valley as a straight NW-SE fault-controlled trough in the south
dendritic dissection of the plateau margin where the rivers leave it

windows.name: bolivian_orocline
windows.title: Bolivian orocline, Salar de Uyuni to Santa Cruz
features: the Altiplano: an internally drained plateau at 3.6-4 km with dead-flat salars (Uyuni, Coipasa)
the Western Cordillera's volcanic cones above 5.5 km on the plateau's western edge
the Eastern Cordillera: deeply incised high ranges (Cordillera Real, near 6.4 km) on the plateau's eastern edge
the Subandean fold-thrust belt: long narrow anticline ridges 15-30 km apart, curving with the orocline
the bend of the Andes from NW-SE to N-S trend between 18 and 20 S
the flat Chaco foreland plain below 500 m to the east around Santa Cruz

windows.name: norwegian_fjords
windows.title: Western Norway's fjords
features: Sognefjord: a 200 km branching trough, 2-5 km wide and over 1.2 km deep, with a shallow sill at its mouth
Hardangerfjord and the fjords of Sunnmore as overdeepened U-shaped troughs cut into a plateau
steep fjord walls rising 1-1.5 km from the water to a high-level plateau surface
Hardangervidda and the Jostedalsbreen plateau: low relief at 1-2 km between the troughs
the strandflat and skerry coast at the outer coast
hanging valleys entering the main troughs high on their walls

windows.name: patagonian_fjords
windows.title: Patagonian fjords and icefields, Chile
features: a maze of fjords, channels and drowned valleys with islands (Chonos archipelago, Wellington Island)
straight north-south channels along the Liquine-Ofqui fault zone
the Northern Patagonian Icefield's plateau (San Valentin, 4 km) near 46.6 S and the Southern Icefield south of 48 S (ice surfaces, unmarked)
glacial lake basins east of the range (General Carrera, O'Higgins) as flat patches at their surface (about 200 m; no bed in the data)
the Taitao peninsula and the Golfo de Penas as the coast's large western bulge and bay
the narrow continental shelf dropping to the Chile trench in the west

windows.name: aleutian_arc
windows.title: Central Aleutian arc across the date line
features: the Aleutian trench about 7 km deep, about 150 km south of the islands and parallel to them
the chain of volcanic islands (Adak, Atka, Amchitka) on a narrow ridge crest
the forearc terrace and slope between the islands and the trench
the Bowers Ridge curving north from the arc near 180 into the Bering Sea
the flat Aleutian abyssal plain of the Bering Sea at about 3.5-4 km to the north
the Pacific plate's seafloor with seamounts south of the trench

windows.name: mariana_arc
windows.title: Mariana trench and arc
features: the Mariana trench, convex to the east, with the Challenger Deep (about 10.9 km) near 11.3 N, 142.2 E
the frontal arc islands (Guam, Rota, Saipan) on the forearc's crest
the active volcanic arc's small islands and seamounts west of the frontal arc
the Mariana Trough back-arc basin opening behind the arc
the West Mariana Ridge, a remnant arc on the trough's western side
seamounts of the old Pacific plate entering the trench from the east

windows.name: indonesian_arcs
windows.title: Banda arc and the eastern Sunda arc, Indonesia
features: the Banda arc's horseshoe: an inner volcanic arc (Flores, Alor, Wetar, the Banda islands) and an outer non-volcanic arc (Timor, Tanimbar, Seram)
the Timor trough (about 3 km) between Timor and the Australian shelf
the Weber Deep, a forearc basin over 7 km deep near 5.5 S, 131.5 E
the Banda Sea's deep basins inside the arc
the Lesser Sunda chain of volcanic islands from Sumbawa to Flores in the west
the shallow Sahul shelf of northern Australia in the south

windows.name: scottish_highlands
windows.title: Scottish Highlands
features: the Great Glen: a straight NE-SW fault valley about 100 km long with Loch Ness
the NE-SW Caledonian grain of ridges and valleys
glacial troughs and sea lochs on the west coast (Loch Linnhe, Loch Hourn)
the Cairngorm plateau: a high (about 1.2 km) low-relief surface
the Highland Boundary Fault's straight front above the Midland Valley in the south
the Inner Hebrides (Skye, Mull) and the Outer Hebrides' low island chain

windows.name: appalachian_fold_belt
windows.title: Appalachian Valley and Ridge, Pennsylvania to Virginia
features: the Valley and Ridge: long parallel ridges 5-10 km apart, a few hundred metres high, NE-SW
zig-zag ridges at plunging fold noses in central Pennsylvania
water gaps where the Susquehanna and the Potomac cut across the ridges
the Allegheny Front escarpment and the dendritic, deeply dissected Appalachian Plateau to the northwest
the Great Valley and the Blue Ridge to the southeast
the Piedmont and the flat Atlantic Coastal Plain in the east

windows.name: canadian_shield_lakes
windows.title: Canadian Shield lakes, northwestern Ontario and Manitoba
features: low relief (under about 150 m) knobby scoured bedrock at 300-500 m
deranged drainage: lakes in structural lows as flat patches at their surface (Lake of the Woods, Lac Seul, Lake Nipigon; no bed in the data)
E-W and NE-SW lineaments of the greenstone belts and faults
the flat glacial Lake Agassiz plain around Lake Winnipeg in the west
the Hudson Bay Lowland's flat plain sloping to the northeast
Lake Superior's north shore escarpment in the southeast, with the lake's bed (to about -180 m) in the data: an enclosed basin below 0 m, drawn as land

windows.name: dalmatian_coast
windows.title: Dalmatian coast and the Dinarides, Croatia
features: a concordant coast: long NW-SE islands (Brac, Hvar, Korcula) and channels parallel to the mountain grain
drowned valleys and the Kornati archipelago as a partly submerged ridge-and-valley landscape
karst ridges rising straight from the sea (Velebit, Biokovo, about 1.7-1.9 km)
poljes: flat-floored closed karst basins inland (Livanjsko polje)
the Dinaric ranges' parallel ridges continuing inland
the shallow Adriatic shelf

windows.name: hawaii
windows.title: Hawaiian Islands
features: the shield volcanoes Mauna Loa and Mauna Kea (4.2 km above sea, about 9 km above the seafloor) with gentle flanks of a few degrees
rift zones as ridges radiating from the summits and continuing under the sea (Puna ridge)
the age progression to the northwest: eroded older islands with deep canyons (Kauai's Waimea) and sea cliffs (Molokai's north coast)
giant submarine landslide deposits (Nuuanu, north of Oahu)
the Hawaiian Deep, a moat around the islands about 5.5 km deep
the insular shelves of the older islands

windows.name: himalaya_nepal
windows.title: Central Himalaya, Nepal
features: the flat Gangetic foreland below 200 m
the Siwalik hills: narrow ridges along the Main Frontal Thrust
the High Himalaya above 8 km (Everest, Kangchenjunga, Dhaulagiri, Annapurna) about 100 km from the foreland
transverse gorges cutting through the range (Kali Gandaki between Dhaulagiri and Annapurna)
the southern Tibetan plateau at 4.5-5 km with the Yarlung Tsangpo valley along its southern edge

windows.name: alps
windows.title: Alps, Jura and Po plain
features: the arcuate range with peaks above 4 km (Mont Blanc, Monte Rosa)
glacial troughs: the Rhone, Rhine, Inn and Adige valleys
perialpine lakes as flat patches at their surface (Geneva, Constance, Como, Garda; no bed in the data)
the Jura's arcuate fold belt in the northwest: anticline ridges 5-10 km apart
the Molasse basin north of the range and the flat Po plain to the south

windows.name: basin_and_range
windows.title: Basin and Range, Nevada and Utah
features: alternating N-S ranges and flat basins about 20-30 km apart: tilted fault blocks
playas and the Bonneville Salt Flats as dead-flat basin floors
Death Valley near 36.3 N, 116.8 W: an enclosed basin down to about -86 m, drawn as land
the Sierra Nevada's steep eastern escarpment in the southwest
the Wasatch front's straight escarpment in the east
